items.summary: A new study combining genomic analyses and fossil evidence sheds light on the century-old "Palaeoptera Problem," a longstanding debate over the evolutionary relationships among major groups of winged insects.

items.title: Messy, risky outdoor play is important for children, but adults can stop them enjoying it
items.summary: There is growing evidence that children today have fewer opportunities for independent, adventurous outdoor play and fewer chances to make decisions and shape their own experiences than previous generations.

items.title: Colorado River drought drives unprecedented pattern of groundwater loss
items.summary: Declining Colorado River flows and falling water levels at Lake Powell and Lake Mead are highly visible signs of the Southwestern megadrought.

items.title: How literature can inspire us to forgive
items.summary: A story that places us inside the mind of a character who is remorseful about causing harm can inspire forgiveness for that fictional bad act, a new study finds.

items.title: Sexual violence survivors often expect systems to fail or harm them, study finds
items.summary: University students who are survivors of sexual violence are forced to perform a constant, exhausting "calculus"—weighing risks, safety, stigma, emotional costs, institutional consequences and likelihood of being believed—when deciding whether and how to seek help.
